summary: Milestone 2026.04.116 completed the supplied operational slice in 40 minutes across 11 completed experiments, averaging 4 minutes per experiment. The slowest-five timing was dominated by recurring gate churn rather than productive GPU-bound work: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 entries gated on the Exp 1414 repair-executor path consumed 25 minutes (62.5%), the legacy Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 gate consumed 10 minutes (25%), and a SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight block consumed 2 minutes (5%). Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, with only 4 MB allocated on each GPU, 0% utilization, and no GPU processes. Estimated next-milestone savings are 55% if same-verdict gates terminalize, readiness checks move to activation time, and independent model lanes use DualGPURunner.
timing_data_caveat: The supplied slowest-experiment labels reference recurring repair/arXiv/cache gate classes from earlier experiment IDs. This artifact treats those labels as authoritative timing evidence for the 2026.04.116 operational slice, while using exp1506-exp1518 only for milestone context.

research_milestone_context.context_summary: Milestone .116 preserved runtime-contract, FR-11 feedback, THRML/KAN/KV260 claim-boundary, and portable trace2skill evidence. This operational retro evaluates execution efficiency rather than research merit.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: The full-pipeline path remained gated on repair-executor availability instead of requiring fresh nonzero accepted-repair evidence or measurable downstream improvement.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: A known legacy publication gate stayed on the runtime critical path instead of terminalizing at activation with explicit unchanged upstream state.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: This was duplicate same-dependency pipeline churn. Once the gate produced a no-improvement verdict, reruns should have been suppressed until the repair artifact changed.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Another repeated pipeline attempt consumed time without evidence of a changed repair executor, candidate pool, or validator contract.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Doomed-rerun block: SOTA GGUF Cache + Provenance Preflight - P
slowest_experiments.why_slow: A cache/provenance readiness failure was discovered as a runtime slot. This should be a fast structured activation preflight with explicit missing-cache and provenance fields.

bottlenecks_identified: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 gate churn consumed 25 of 40 minutes (62.5%) across three slowest-five entries.
The Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 legacy gate consumed 10 minutes (25%) despite being a recurring known-blocked publication path.
The SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight still appeared as a doomed-rerun execution slot instead of an activation-time readiness artifact.
GPU utilization was inefficient for any LLM-bearing work: both RTX 3090s were idle with 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization.
No material GPU zombie processes were present; the resource issue was idle scheduler capacity, not leaked VRAM.
Several .116 tracks could have overlapped: safe-DSL induction and trigger/grammar certificate work, product-line solver and plan-graph contract checks, plus THRML/KAN/KV260 source-level lanes.
The FR-11 policy cache -> rollback -> portable skill pack chain was truly sequential, but unrelated hardware/source-level and runtime-contract tasks did not need to wait on it.
The pre-flight suite was not the dominant wall-time bottleneck in the supplied data, but known-blocked preflights still wasted runtime by rediscovering readiness failures.
Documentation reconciliation was not a top-five timing item, but exp1518 explicitly deferred ops docs to a separate reconciliation pass, creating avoidable closeout handoff overhead.
Recent changelog history contains duplicate experiment rows, indicating docs appenders are append-only but not sufficiently idempotent.
improvements_suggested: Require nonzero accepted-repair evidence or nonzero pipeline improvement before scheduling Full-Scale Pipeline reruns.
Add same-verdict retirement for repeated Full-Scale Pipeline gate attempts within a milestone.
Terminalize Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 and SOTA GGUF cache/provenance readiness at activation time unless their upstream state changed.
Persist before/after gpu_monitor.py snapshots in every GPU-bearing result artifact, including process count, utilization, VRAM, and DualGPURunner lane assignment.
Use DualGPURunner by default for independent Qwen/Gemma local SOTA checks when both RTX 3090s are free.
Parallelize independent .116-style lanes after phase-0 gates: safe-DSL vs grammar certificates, plan-graph vs product-line solver, and THRML/KAN/KV260 source-level checks.
Keep global preflight checks cluster-scoped until full-suite/spec-coverage debt is green enough for blanket gating.
Make docs reconciliation a no-op-aware command keyed by milestone and experiment id so changelog and roadmap rows are appended exactly once.
Store a structured conductor timing ledger with categories for gate wait, preflight, GPU inference, CPU analysis, docs reconciliation, and artifact write time.
Require operational-retro prompts to carry a milestone-local timing snapshot so retros do not need to infer current efficiency from older experiment labels.
savings_basis: The supplied slowest five account for 37 of 40 minutes. Not all 37 minutes can be removed because terminal gate artifacts and small diagnostics still have real cost, but eliminating duplicate pipeline churn, terminalizing legacy arXiv/cache checks, and overlapping independent work should plausibly recover about 22 minutes.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Terminalize repeated Full-Scale Pipeline same-verdict gates
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: Three Full-Scale Pipeline v3 entries dominated the timing. Reruns should require changed repair evidence or nonzero downstream improvement.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Move arXiv and SOTA GGUF readiness checks to activation-time terminal artifacts
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: The 10 minute arXiv gate and 2 minute cache/provenance block are known readiness states that should not consume scheduled runtime slots.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Enforce DualGPURunner and timing telemetry for independent model lanes
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: Both RTX 3090s were idle with no GPU processes. Telemetry plus lane assignment would expose missed parallelism and prevent silent sequential fallback.

questions_answered.which_experiments_took_the_longest_and_w: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor was the dominant path: 14, 6, and 5 minute entries totaling 25 minutes because the gate allowed repeated pipeline validation without new nonzero repair evidence. arXiv Bundle v10 gated on Exp 1269 consumed another 10 minutes as a recurring legacy publication gate. The SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight consumed 2 minutes rediscovering a known readiness failure.
questions_answered.was_gpu_utilization_efficient_sequential: No. The supplied and verified gpu_monitor.py snapshots show both RTX 3090s at 4/24576 MB and 0% utilization with no compute processes. Any live Qwen/Gemma model lanes should have used DualGPURunner across GPU 0 and GPU 1, while CPU-only source-level tasks ran independently.
questions_answered.were_there_zombie_processes_wasting_reso: No. gpu_monitor.py reported an empty process list and no warnings. The residual 4 MB allocation per GPU is below the script's zombie threshold and is consistent with driver/context residue, not material VRAM waste.
questions_answered.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. The .116 DAG had independent lanes: safe-DSL induction could overlap with trigger/grammar certificate work, product-line solver work could overlap with plan-graph contract checks, and THRML/KAN/KV260 source-level checks could run independently. The FR-11 policy cache to rollback to portable skill pack path was legitimately sequential.
questions_answered.was_the_preflight_test_suite_a_bottlenec: Not the dominant bottleneck in the supplied timing. Only 2 minutes of the slowest five are directly preflight-like, versus 25 minutes for pipeline gate churn and 10 minutes for the arXiv gate. The preflight system still needs activation-time terminal artifacts for known readiness failures.
questions_answered.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: They were not measured as a slowest-five bottleneck, but they were operationally inefficient because the .116 research retro deferred ops docs to a separate reconciliation agent and recent changelog history shows duplicate append rows. Idempotent docs appenders would reduce closeout friction.
questions_answered.what_tooling_infrastructure_changes_woul: Nonzero-success gates, same-verdict retirement, activation-time readiness artifacts, DualGPURunner lane assignment, per-experiment GPU telemetry, cluster-scoped preflight, structured conductor timing categories, and idempotent changelog/roadmap appenders.

preflight_suite.assessment: The preflight suite was not the main timing bottleneck in this slice, but readiness checks should become fast terminal artifacts rather than scheduled doomed reruns.

doc_reconciliation.assessment: Manual docs reconciliation was short but structurally avoidable. The conductor should expose an idempotent docs closeout command that appends changelog and roadmap rows exactly once.

meta_reflection: The milestone is already short in absolute terms, so the remaining win is mostly scheduler discipline rather than faster agents. The conductor needs stronger evidence boundaries: available is not the same as useful, blocked is not the same as worth rediscovering, and GPU-ready hardware is not the same as GPU-used execution.
